items.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Is that Kay Norton? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. It cost me a pretty penny, but I got it back, and he’s still my attorney.

ctx.x: Anyway, he and I split. Then he went on with the company, and I got my own company. Later on, he just got out of the music business. He was teaching school over there in Brooklyn, I think. Then he moved back to Florida. That’s where he died. Then what I did – what I wisely did – oh yeah. Then you find people taking advantage of you. When we had the Jazztet together, we had a manager. She liked us so well, she never charged us or anything. But then she fell on hard times. After the fact, I found out that she had…
Yeah. It cost me a pretty penny, but I got it back, and he’s still my attorney. At that time, he was Liberace’s attorney. So he knew the business. He’s still my attorney and we . . .
